facts.setup: In 1981, Bernie Sanders was elected mayor of Burlington by a margin of exactly ___ votes.
facts.sourceTitle: Seven Days: Viva La Bernie! Sanderista Revolution Turns 30
facts.sourceQuote: Sanders was elected mayor of Burlington by an eventual 10-vote margin in a three-way race against Democrat Gordon Paquette.

facts.setup: In 1987, while still mayor of Burlington, Bernie Sanders recorded ___.
facts.answer: a folk album ("We Shall Overcome," backed by Vermont musicians)
facts.sourceTitle: Seven Days: Bernie Sanders Recorded a Folk Album. No Punchline Required
facts.sourceQuote: In 1987, while serving as Burlington's mayor, Sanders recorded an album of folk classics for the defunct BurlingTown Recordings label.

facts.setup: Since 1988, Burlington's official sister city has been ___.
facts.sourceTitle: VTDigger: Burlington suspends relationship with its Russian sister city
facts.sourceQuote: The two cities have had a sister city relationship since 1988 through the independent nonprofit Burlington-Yaroslavl Sister City Program.

facts.setup: In 1979, Winooski's city planners applied for a federal grant to study covering the entire city with ___.
facts.sourceTitle: VTDigger: The Winooski Dome: How this mill town was almost sealed in a bubble
facts.sourceQuote: Winooski's ingenious city planners applied for a $55,000 federal grant to study the possibility of constructing a dome over the city.

facts.setup: In 1982, the Vermont House passed a resolution officially protecting ___ from "death, injury, or harassment."
facts.sourceTitle: Vermont Historical Society (Green Mountaineer): Vermont's Very Own Monster
facts.sourceQuote: the Vermont House of Representatives passed a resolution in April of 1982 which states that Champ should be protected from willful acts resulting in death, injury, or harassment.

facts.setup: In the 1800s, circus showman P.T. Barnum offered $50,000 to anyone who could ___.
facts.sourceTitle: Vermont Historical Society (Green Mountaineer): Vermont's Very Own Monster
facts.sourceQuote: Despite frequent Champ spottings like these in the 1800s no one claimed the $50,000 that circus promoter P.T. Barnum offered as a reward for the creature's capture.

facts.setup: The most famous photo of Champ was snapped in July 1977 by a vacationing Connecticut woman named ___.
facts.sourceTitle: Vermont Historical Society (Green Mountaineer): Vermont's Very Own Monster
facts.sourceQuote: But it was the July, 1977, sighting of Champ by Sandra Mansi that was so remarkable... Sandra Mansi had a camera and was able to snap a picture of the creature before it disappeared beneath the water.

facts.setup: The Battle of Bennington was actually fought in ___.
facts.answer: New York (Walloomsac, just over the border)
facts.sourceTitle: Vermont Historical Society (Green Mountaineer): Vermont Trivia
facts.sourceQuote: No, the Battle of Bennington was not fought in Bennington. No, it was not even fought in the state of Vermont. It was fought in Wallomsack, New York, just over the border from Vermont and only a few miles from Bennington.

facts.setup: Burlington's 40-foot-tall filing-cabinet sculpture has 38 drawers — one for every year that ___.
facts.answer: the Southern Connector highway project sat unbuilt (1965 to 2002)
facts.sourceTitle: Seven Days: WTF: What's With the File Cabinet Tower on Burlington's Flynn Avenue?
facts.sourceQuote: an installation created by Burlington architect Bren Alvarez ... [38 drawers,] one for each year from 1965 to 2002 ... titled 'File Under So. Co., Waiting for…'

facts.setup: Burlington's beloved winged-monkey statues were originally made in 1975 to advertise ___.
facts.answer: a waterbed store called The Emerald City of Oz
facts.sourceTitle: Burlington City Arts: Winged Monkeys
facts.sourceQuote: The Winged Monkeys of the clock tower were originally made in 1975 for a waterbed store in downtown Burlington called 'The Emerald City of Oz.'

facts.setup: At Phish's first-ever show — a 1983 UVM dorm dance — the band's microphone stand was ___.
facts.sourceTitle: Phish.com official tour archive: Fri 1983-12-02, Harris/Millis Cafeteria, UVM
facts.sourceQuote: This was Phish's (Trey Anastasio, Jon Fishman, Mike Gordon and Jeff Holdsworth) 1st show ... A hockey stick was used as a microphone stand.

facts.setup: In 2014, Burlington became the first city in America to ___.
facts.answer: source 100% of its power from renewable generation
facts.sourceTitle: Burlington Electric Department (city utility) press release
facts.sourceQuote: In 2014, Burlington became the first city in the nation to source 100% of its power from renewable generation

facts.setup: The face on the cover of Phish's 1992 major-label debut album belongs to ___.
facts.answer: Nectar Rorris, the Burlington bar owner who gave them their start (the album is "A Picture of Nectar")
facts.sourceTitle: Seven Days: Nectar's, a Burlington Landmark, at 40
facts.sourceQuote: featured on their 1992 major-label debut A Picture of Nectar, the album that bore Rorris' face on its cover.

facts.setup: In 1998, Lake Champlain was legally one of the Great Lakes — for exactly ___.
facts.sourceTitle: UVM Lake Champlain Sea Grant: Why isn't Lake Champlain a Great Lake?
facts.sourceQuote: On March 6, 1998, President Clinton signed a bill drafted by U.S. Senator Patrick Leahy of Vermont... The bill included a single line declaring Lake Champlain a Great Lake... Only 18 days after the bill passed, Lake Champlain's Great Lake status was rescinded.

facts.setup: Before opening their first shop in a converted Burlington gas station in 1978, Ben and Jerry learned to make ice cream from ___.
facts.sourceTitle: WCAX: This Day in History: A $5 ice cream class sparks the Ben & Jerry's empire
facts.sourceQuote: The two friends had taken a $5 ice cream-making course at Penn State, then decided to turn what they learned into a business. ... On May 5, 1978, Ben Cohen and Jerry Greenfield launched the very first Ben & Jerry's ice cream shop in a converted gas station in downtown Burlington.

facts.setup: In 1955, the 220-foot steamboat Ticonderoga traveled from Lake Champlain to the Shelburne Museum by ___.
facts.answer: being hauled overland on railroad tracks for two months — never more than 250 feet a day
facts.sourceTitle: VTDigger: Ticonderoga celebrates 70 years on land
facts.sourceQuote: It took a little over two months to move the boat, which had been chugging around Lake Champlain since it was built in 1906 at the Shelburne shipyard. It never moved more than 250 feet in a day.

facts.setup: Buried beside UVM's Ira Allen Chapel are the ashes of ___.
facts.sourceTitle: VTDigger: Then Again: Burlington-born John Dewey was education reformer, and more
facts.sourceQuote: John Dewey's ashes are buried beside Ira Allen Chapel at UVM, where he earned his undergraduate degree.

facts.setup: Resting on the bottom of Burlington Bay is the only archaeologically studied American ferry that was powered by ___.
facts.sourceTitle: Lake Champlain Maritime Museum: Horse Ferry
facts.sourceQuote: The fragile horse-powered ferry in Burlington Bay is the only archaeologically studied example of a turntable 'team-boat' ... The Burlington Bay Horse Ferry was discovered in the fall of 1983 during a side-scan sonar survey.

facts.setup: The letters UVM don't stand for "University of Vermont" — they're short for ___.
facts.answer: Universitas Viridis Montis, Latin for "University of the Green Mountains"
facts.sourceTitle: UVM Catalogue: About the University
facts.sourceQuote: This popular abbreviation is derived from the Latin Universitas Viridis Montis, University of the Green Mountains.

facts.setup: For about 75 years, the Winooski River was officially known as the ___ River.
facts.answer: Onion (Winooski is Abenaki for the wild onions on its banks)
facts.sourceTitle: Seven Days: What's in a Name? The Origins of the "Winooski" River
facts.sourceQuote: 'Onion River' remained the prevailing designation for the 75 years or so after Vermont became first an independent republic and, later, a state. ... some residents of Vermont's capital city were fretting over the fact that their community was known as Montpelier-on-the-Onion.

facts.setup: Since 1968, it has been illegal everywhere in Vermont to put up ___.
facts.sourceTitle: VTDigger: Then Again: Vermont's billboard ban followed a winding road to passage
facts.sourceQuote: Vermont became the first state in the continental United States to ban billboards. ... Billboard companies and advertisers labeled efforts to ban the signs 'communist.'

facts.setup: Burlington-born First Lady Grace Coolidge married Calvin Coolidge in ___.
facts.answer: her parents' home at 312 Maple Street, Burlington
facts.sourceTitle: Vermont State Historic Sites: Ethan Allen Monument
facts.sourceQuote: buried in this cemetery are the parents of First Lady Grace Goodhue Coolidge, who was born in Burlington and later married President Calvin Coolidge in her parent's home at 312 Maple Street.

facts.setup: The hottest temperature ever recorded in Burlington — set back in August 1944 — is ___ degrees.
facts.sourceTitle: National Weather Service Burlington: Burlington, Vermont Temperature Extremes
facts.sourceQuote: Highest 101 degrees on August 11th, 1944

facts.setup: The first ski rope tow in the United States was started by three local families in ___, Vermont.
facts.sourceTitle: Vermont Historical Society: First Ski Tow in the U.S.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1935, they started running the first rope tow in the United States.

facts.setup: By Vermont law, anyone serving apple pie must make a "good faith" effort to serve it with ___.
facts.answer: a glass of cold milk, at least half an ounce of cheddar cheese, or a large scoop of vanilla ice cream
facts.sourceTitle: Vermont Acts of the 1999-2000 Legislature, No. 15 (official archive)
facts.sourceQuote: Sec. 2. SERVING APPLE PIE — When serving apple pie in Vermont, a "good faith" effort shall be made to meet one or more of the following conditions: (a) with a glass of cold milk, (b) with a slice of cheddar cheese weighing a minimum of 1/2 ounce, (c) with a large scoop of vanilla ice cream.

facts.setup: The number-one-selling curry brand in Japan is named ___.
facts.answer: Vermont Curry (flavored with apple and honey)
facts.sourceTitle: House Foods Group: Vermont Curry (official product site)
facts.sourceQuote: Vermont Curry is the number-one selling brand of Japanese curry roux. ... The origin of 'Vermont' in Vermont Curry dates back to a book entitled 'Folk Medicine: A Vermont Doctor's Guide to Good Health.'

facts.setup: The first person ever to photograph a snowflake was a Vermonter from ___.
facts.sourceTitle: Vermont Historical Society: Snowflake Bentley
facts.sourceQuote: Wilson Alwyn Bentley otherwise known as Snowflake Bentley of Jericho, Vermont had a fascination with nature and meteorology. His captivation with snowflakes, ultimately, led him to be the first individual to capture a picture of a snowflake in 1885.

facts.setup: Vermont's official state fossil is ___.
facts.answer: a beluga whale skeleton, dug up by railroad workers in Charlotte in 1849
facts.sourceTitle: UVM Natural History Collections: The Charlotte Whale
facts.sourceQuote: The whale skeleton was originally unearthed near Charlotte, Vermont in 1849 by railroad workers during construction of the first railroad between Rutland and Burlington. ... The whale was declared the official State Fossil in 1993, and the bill was signed into law by Governor Howard Dean.

facts.setup: Isle La Motte in Lake Champlain is home to the world's oldest known ___.
facts.answer: reef built by a community of organisms — about 480 million years old
facts.sourceTitle: Lake Champlain Committee: Lake Champlain's Ancient Chazy Fossil Reef
facts.sourceQuote: the Chazy Reef is the oldest known reef on Earth built by a community of different organisms ... About 480 million years ago... an expansive tropical sea teemed with life.

facts.setup: When President Harding died in 1923, Calvin Coolidge was sworn in at 2:47 a.m. in Plymouth Notch, Vermont, by ___.
facts.answer: his own father, a notary public — by the light of a kerosene lamp
facts.sourceTitle: Seven Days: Plymouth Notch Marks the Centennial of Calvin Coolidge's Presidential Inauguration
facts.sourceQuote: By the light of a kerosene lamp, with his late mother's Bible nearby, Coolidge raised his right hand and swore to preserve, protect and defend the Constitution. (Article: his father, Col. John Coolidge, a notary public, administered the oath at 2:47 a.m. on August 3, 1923.)

facts.setup: Vermont's official state beverage, on the books since 1983, is ___.
facts.sourceTitle: Vermont Statutes Online, 1 V.S.A. § 503
facts.sourceQuote: § 503. State Beverage — The State Beverage shall be milk. (Added 1983, No. 22, § 1, eff. April 22, 1983.)

facts.setup: Vermont's official state animal is ___.
facts.sourceTitle: Vermont Statutes Online, 1 V.S.A. § 500
facts.sourceQuote: § 500. State Animal — The State Animal shall be the Morgan horse. (1961, No. 42, § 1, eff. March 23, 1961.)

facts.setup: Among Vermont's official state emblems is an official state ___ — the "Tunbridge series."
facts.sourceTitle: Vermont Statutes Online, 1 V.S.A. § 504
facts.sourceQuote: § 504. State Soil — The State Soil shall be the Tunbridge soil series. (Added 1985, No. 9, § 1, eff. Mar. 27, 1985.)

facts.setup: The real Sound of Music family bought a Stowe farmhouse for the view — and the following spring, the house ___.
facts.sourceTitle: Seven Days: With a Run of Concerts at Trapp Family Lodge, 'The Sound of Music' Comes Home
facts.sourceQuote: They bought the view — and the house partially collapsed during a blizzard the following spring. (Also: 'the von Trapp family settled in 1942 and where descendants still operate a sprawling hospitality business.')

facts.setup: Back when Vermont was an independent republic, it ran its own mint in the town of Rupert, producing ___.
facts.sourceTitle: Vermont Historical Society: This Place in History: Harmon's Mint
facts.sourceQuote: Vermont's only official mint was located in Rupert, VT. Started by Reuben Harmon, Jr. it ran from 1785 to 1788, producing just two copper coin designs for the then Republic of Vermont.

facts.setup: Church Street Marketplace was modeled on a famous pedestrian street in ___.
facts.sourceTitle: Church Street Marketplace: History
facts.sourceQuote: In 1962, architecture student Bill Truex experienced the transformation of Strøget, Copenhagen's main shopping center, that went from a 'traffic-snarled nightmare' to a successful pedestrian mall. ... The Church Street Marketplace officially opened as we know it today on September 15, 1981

facts.setup: In September 1941 — months before Pearl Harbor — the Vermont Legislature declared that the state was already ___.
facts.answer: in "armed conflict" with Germany (so drafted Vermonters could collect a bonus)
facts.sourceTitle: VTDigger: Then Again: Vermont aids the Allies in the run-up to World War II
facts.sourceQuote: Eighty years ago, in September 1941, the Vermont Legislature declared that the state was already in 'armed conflict' with Germany.

facts.setup: The last known wild catamount in Vermont was killed in ___.
facts.sourceTitle: Vermont Historical Society: Last Catamount in Vermont
facts.sourceQuote: The last known catamount in Vermont was killed in 1881.

facts.setup: At Lone Rock Point in Burlington, geologists from around the world come to see rock layers that are famously ___.
facts.answer: stacked in the wrong order — older rock sitting on top of younger rock
facts.sourceTitle: Vermont Geological Survey (DEC): Champlain Thrust at Lone Rock Point, Burlington
facts.sourceQuote: The thrust is a Middle Ordovician, east-dipping fault along which older Cambrian rocks have been placed on top of younger Ordovician rocks, with an estimated throw of 8,850 feet at Lone Rock Point.

facts.setup: Montpelier is the only state capital in America without ___.
facts.sourceTitle: Seven Days: Figure It Out: Summing Up Vermont by the Numbers
facts.sourceQuote: Montpelier was estimated at only 7,592, making it the smallest state capital in the country — and the only one without a McDonald's.
